HYPERPOP!

HISTORY: A LITTLE RUNDOWN

what exactly is "hyperpop"?:

Hyperpop is a subgenre of electronic music, incorporating heavy synths, auto-tuned vocals, bright electronic textures and most of the time, including experimental aspects in them. Throughout the years, it has seen a rise in popularity, with an abundance of artists appearing now more than ever, taking inspiration from other popular genres, such as cloud rap, j-pop, hip hop, dubstep etc., slowly cementing its place in the mainstream music scene.

earliest days/2010s:

At its earliest, hyperpop wasn't actually called hyperpop. It had many aliases, but it was referred to most frequently as 'bubblegum bass' (which is still its own genre now). The first group to inspire the hyperpop genre was indisputibly made by PC Music, a label created by A. G. Cook, with artists including Hannah Diamond, GFOTY, Danny L Harle and more. PC Music then pushed the boundaries of pop music, with PC Music Volumes 1-3, placing a foundation for hyperpop as a genre to bloom. SOPHIE, another A. G. Cook collaborator, started to rise in popularity, working with many artists from PC Music, releasing many singles that shifted the direction of the genre.

start of a first wave/late 2010s

After a short time of hyperpop 'dying down', a new wave emerged for the genre in 2019, inspired by the duo 100 gecs. Their debut album inspired Spotify to launch a 'Hyperpop' playlist, which pretty much was the beginning of the genre being unanimously called hyperpop.

tiktok

The overwhelming popularity of TikTok in 2020 ignited by the COVID-19 pandemic, also helped push the genre even further. Trends which included songs similar or adjacent to hyperpop, such as #BrooklynBloodPop by Syko or SugarCrash! by ElyOtto started to blow up due to many users discovering it while doomscrolling. Although many listeners were one-off ones, many stayed to be fans of the genre. Ayesha Erotica was also a prominent figure in the TikTok era, with many creators choosing her songs. Along with Charli XCX's "how i'm feeling now" album, many new, younger fans were exposed to the genre, creating a brand new generation.

mainstream hyperpop/2023-4

The release of Charli's 2024 album, "Brat", Porter Robinson's "SMILE!:D", and Underscores's "Wallsocket" absolutely blew up the hyperpop scene. Porter, being a prominent figure in electronic music already, introduced many fans to hyperpop through his album dabbling in elements of hyperpop. Meanwhile, Charli's already big fanbase grew larger and larger as songs off "Brat" blew up online, on almost every single media platform. These releases pushed the genre into 'mainstream' status. Despite this newfound popularity, the genre seemed to come to a standstill, due to many mainstream artists afraid to try new things. Thus, a new generation came into the picture.

DID YOU KNOW?

in 2014, Cook, SOPHIE, and British singer Harriet Pittard worked together to create "Hey QT", made to advertise an energy drink.

The song "#BrooklynBloodPop", used in many TikTok gaming clips, dance/lipsync videos and edits.

DID YOU KNOW?

Tell Me(U Want It) off of "U", the latest studio album by Underscores was recently credited as the best song of 2026 so far by Spotify (as of 18 June)!

Current time/2024-present

Now, the hyperpop genre is being newly redefined by a close network of smaller, highly experimental artists. This could arguably be the reason why the term 'hyperpop' is so loosely defined nowadays, as all these artists take heavy inspiration from other genres, such as rock, metal, rage rap etc. However all being tied together by the influence from hyperpop. Artists such as Underscores, Jane Remover, Femtanyl, Glaive and Frost Children are all such examples of the new wave of the genre.

In 2024, 2Hollis opened for rapper and Playboi Carti affiliate, Ken Carson's tour. This introduced fans of rage rap, the genre Ken is most known for, to EDM/hyperpop. As a result, many artists started to blend both genres together. Some examples of artists blowing up due to this blend of genres are Lucy Bedroque, Kuru and Slayr.

In 2025, Slayr released "Half Blood", and Lucy Bedroque released "Unmusique". (Slayr also released a deluxe in 2026, featuring Lucy.) These albums led to a split in the underground rage rap community, as both artists despite using rage rap in the majority, still had elements of EDM, hyperpop and digicore. Many fans of traditional rage rap called Slayr's music "Burger Music", for incorporating these elements. To this day, the hyperpop scene has been on Slayr's side, with artists working with him, such as Tiffany Day and Underscores, or co-signing him, such as Ninajirachi.

In 2026, artist Matt Proxy dissed popular Korean boy band CORTIS, and almost every other K-pop group. This caused yet another shift in the community, as Slayr tweeted, "shout out cortis", and Matt calling him out for it. Up till now, nothing has really happened to fix this.

DID YOU KNOW?

The genre has achieved a Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 single before, being Sam Smith and Kim Petras's "Unholy".

Jane Remover and Underscores have appeared in Charli XCX's concerts in London, and USA respectively.

DID YOU KNOW?

Hyperpop was featured in a Google doodle before, during June 2025, for Pride Month.

NOTABLE ARTISTS!

Porter Robinson

Porter Weston Robinson is an American singer-songwriter and producer. His debut album "Worlds", released in 2014 was number 1 on Billboard's Top Dance/Electronic Albums. His influence in the current Electronic and Hyperpop scene is undeniable, with third studio album "Smile!:D" being a worldwide hit. He also worked with hit game League of Legends, to create the song: "Everything Goes On". He also collaborates with other hyperpop artists, like Ninajirachi.

100 gecs

100 Gecs, an American musical duo formed in 2015, consists of Dylan Brady and Laura Les. Their debut studio album "1000 gecs" was an instant hit, albeit it being divisive. The album helped to consolidate the eclectic "hyperpop" style by taking the genre to its most extreme, and extremely catchy, conclusions: stadium-sized trap beats processed and distorted to near-destruction, overwrought emo vocals and cascades of ravey arpeggios. The duo also DJ'd for the game Minecraft, which helped to push their fame further. Collaborations with other artists like Cook, Charli and more helped to push their sound even further.

Glaive

Glaive, an American singer-songwriter, rose to prominence when he posted multiple singles on soundcloud around 2020. He then signed a record deal with Interscope Records. He regularly appeared on Spotify's hyperpop playlists, making him even more known. He collaborated with fellow artist Ericdoa, touring together with him. In 2022, he opened for popular singer The Kid Laroi, after having his first headline tour. Using indie rock, midwest emo, he inspired many others to follow suit and make their own sound.

Charli XCX

Charli XCX is a British singer-songwriter. She started off in the UK rave scene in 2010, and had her first UK number 1 hit, "I Love it" with Icona Pop, and her first worldwide hit, "Fancy" with Iggy Azalea. She then started to work with Cook for PC music, and had him be executive producer for her next albums, "Charli" and "how i'm feeling now". Her biggest work was her sixth studio album, "Brat". This album sent shockwaves throughout the internet, even getting features from Ariana Grande, and Billie Eilish. This album won her three Grammy Awards, and accelerated hyperpop into the mainstream. Being such an important figure in the scene, she is truly an icon of our time.

SOPHIE

Sophie Xeon, more commonly known as SOPHIE, was a British producer-songwriter. Often regarded to some as the 'queen of hyperpop', SOPHIE, along with A. G. Cook, helped to pioneer the genre. Her breakthrough came in a time where she released a run of singles. Her debut album, "Oil of Every Pearl's Un-Insides" was nominated for the Grammy Award for best Dance/Electronic Album. SOPHIE also produced many hits for artists such as Madonna, Vince Staples and Charli XCX. She is one of the first transgender artists to rise to fame, inspiring many others, before her untimely passing on 30th January 2021.

A. G. Cook

Alexander Guy Cook, more commonly known as A. G. Cook is a British producer. Creator of the label PC Music, the style of exaggerated pop pushed by the label helped to serve as a foundation for hyperpop. Cook worked with SOPHIE, Charli XCX, being executive producer for Charli's many albums. Cook's first two albums came in 2020, 7G and Apple, both bringing in much praise, and inspiring many people to explore the genre. He also won the Variety Hitmakers Innovator of The Year Award in 2020.

Jane Remover

Jane Remover, an American rapper, singer and producer, rose to fame during 2021, releasing her debut album "Frailty". The album explored progressive pop and digicore, while her second album "Census Designated" explored shoegaze and rock. Her solidification as an artist in the hyperpop scene came, however, when she released "Revengeseekerz", her third studio album and her second EP "♡", shortly after. These projects used a variety of genres, mostly rap. Jane also created a new microgenre, Dariacore, named after albums she put out. Being one of the current most influential figures in the scene, many people fell in love with her complex production, catchy melodies and aesthetic.

SIMILAR GENRES

BUBBLEGUM BASS

Bubblegum Bass (sometimes referred to as PC Music), is an experimental style of electronic music. The genre was founded in 2013, with A. G. Cook's label, PC Music, drawing influence from the 90s. The genre has been credited as the first era of hyperpop, which it eventually evolved into. Artists like Hannah Diamond, GFOTY and SOPHIE are musicians most relevant to the genre.

Digicore

Digicore is another microgenre that developed around the same time as hyperpop, from the late 2010s to the early 2020s, with quite a lot of parallels. The term digicore was actually created by an online community of teen musicians, through Discord. Rising in popularity during COVID-19, the genre takes inspiration from trap, using many hi-hats, thick autotune and heavy 808 bass. Artists like Slayr, Lucy Bedroque and Kuru popularised the genre.

Glitchcore

Glitchcore is yet another microgenre that developed alongside hyperpop. Glitchcore is defined by heavy audio effects, autotune and chopped vocals, giving it that "glitch" feel. It was once labeled as "hyperpop on steroids", with many similarities to hyperpop, yet having many exaggerated elements. Glitchcore is often paired with fast-paced edits, usually with strobe warnings. These edits frequently appear on TikTok, featuring songs of the genre. Artists like Brakence, Ericdoa and Glaive are commonly associated with the genre.

Dariacore

Dariacore is a subgenre of electronic dance music. Created by Jane Remover, the term Dariacore was named after her album, released using her other alias, leroy. Dariacore itself is named after Daria Morgendorffer, a fictional character in the series "Daria". The genre encompasses sped up and pitch-shifted samples from pop music and other media, as well as influence from mainly breakbeats and jersey club, but could contain almost every genre out there. Artists such as Jane and xeav use this genre.

Hyper-rock

Hyper-rock is a genre that fuses rock and hyperpop. It uses guitar as the main instrument, using the glitchy textures and heavily autotuned vocals from hyperpop. Usually made using rock guitars as a foundation, it is commonly put together with the genre shoegaze. The genre reflects a fusion of influences from a wide variety of genres, being probably the most experimental out of the bunch. Artists/Groups like Quadeca, Jane Remover and Kero Kero Bonito are most commonly associated with this genre.
